question: Who introduced the Zamindari Settlement as a measure of land revenue administration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Cornwallis.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** introduced the **Zamindari Settlement** in **1793 **as a measure of** land revenue administration **in British India.
 
• The Zamindari Settlement was a system of** land revenue collection** where the **East India Company **granted the zamindars (landlords) the right to collect revenue from the peasants in exchange for a **fixed amount of revenue** paid to the Company.
 
• The system was criticized for its** exploitation of peasants** by the **zamindars** and for perpetuating the feudal system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Lytton** introduced the infamous **Vernacular Press Act in 1878,** which curbed the freedom of the press in India and led to widespread protests.
 
• **Lord Curzon** was known for his administrative reforms in India, including the** partition of Bengal in 1905**, which sparked nationalist movements.
 
• **Lord Wellesley** was the **Governor-General of India** from **1798 to 1805** and is known for his** expansionist policies and the Subsidiary Alliance** system, which made Indian states dependent on the British.
 
• **Lord Cornwallis **was also responsible for introducing the **Permanent Settlement in Bengal,** which fixed the revenue to be paid by landowners to the Company, but led to the impoverishment of the peasants.
